notes: Answer to instagram.com/reel/DbVnOOksf-c (alumaetg, an Iranian aluminium lighting-profile maker, 28s, 63k views). Their reel is a 3D assembly animation of an aluminium extrusion — LED strip in, diffuser in, end cap, ceiling mount, finished pendant — under a direct-from-manufacturer caption: every stage in-house, no middlemen. Rameez: change the material to wood. That claim is literally true for NixWoods, and NixWoods has the thing Aluma had to fake in CGI: real footage of a craftsman finishing the wood. So the cut runs assembly (generated + derived stills) then PROOF (real workshop footage), which is the opposite order to theirs and the stronger half last. Hook scores 9/12. BUILT AT ZERO COST: the ElevenLabs image quota ran out after two stages, so stages 3-5 are derived from stage 2 in numpy and ffmpeg rather than generated — the diffuser beat blurs the LED dots into a continuous line, the lit beat screen-composites a warm bloom off the brightest pixels. The three assembly transitions are render_before_after wipes between consecutive stages, which is how a part appears to go into place without generating video of it. First use of the new `wipe` shot type in quickcut.
name: L1-linear-wood
